content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: Triggered P1 - model-catalog-service - model-config-mismatch. Reason: default_revision != pinned_revision for model 'redwood-open-7b-v2'.

pagerduty: Alert details: 
- Service: model-catalog-service
- Severity: P1
- Trigger: catalog_validator; matcher: revision-mismatch
- Alert ID: PD-872341

sara (oncall): acked PD-872341 :white_check_mark:

mike (eng-runtime): on it. seeing a spike in 500s from inference gateway too? could be falling back to incompatible tokenizer.

alice (platform): Confirming — the catalog shows default_revision=rev-2026-03-14 but pinned_revision in deployments is rev-2026-02-28 for most routes. That discrepancy will cause tokenization/embedding mismatch for some models.

raj (sre): Any signs of customer impact metrics? latency, error rate?

julia (support): Customer ticket count up from 2 -> 27 in past 10m referencing garbled outputs and truncated responses. One enterprise customer reported full request failures.

mike (eng-runtime): digging logs. sample error from runtime: 

```
ERROR inference_gateway: tokenizer mismatch: model instance expects tokenizer v1.3, manifest lists v1.5; KV cache invalidation failure; decode exceptions
context: request_id=req-45f3c, model=redwood-open-7b-v2, revision=rev-2026-03-14
```

mike (eng-runtime): Also seeing increased CPU + OOMs on a subset of GPU hosts — likely due to different tokenization changing sequence lengths and memory usage.

sara (oncall): Paging escalation plan: can someone revert default_revision to rev-2026-02-28 in catalog so runtime picks compatible tokenizer? We should also set a temporary routing policy to dedicated pool for affected customers.

alice (platform): I can change catalog default, but need approval for emergency write to catalog-store. What is the safe revert command?

mike (eng-runtime): Run follow-up validation before announce: 
```
# preview what would change
curl -s -X GET "https://catalog.internal/api/v1/models/redwood-open-7b-v2?revision=rev-2026-02-28" | jq '.revision, .tokenizer_version'
```
If tokenizer_version matches pinned deployments -> safe. If matches, then do update with PATCH.

alice (platform): I ran the preview: pinned deployments show tokenizer_version: "v1.3" for rev-2026-02-28, current default shows v1.5. Safe to revert.

sara (oncall): Proceed with revert. Notify me when done. Also add in catalog metadata an emergency "do-not-auto-upgrade" flag.

alice (platform): Performing PATCH now (audit note: emergency revert).

```
PATCH /api/v1/models/redwood-open-7b-v2
{ "default_revision": "rev-2026-02-28", "metadata": { "emergency_do_not_auto_upgrade": "true" } }
```

alice (platform): PATCH complete. catalog-store ack id cs-5401.

mike (eng-runtime): Kicking the compatibility reconciler to reload model routing. command: 
```
./tools/reconciler --model redwood-open-7b-v2 --reload
```

mike (eng-runtime): reconciler reports: new default revision applied to routing table. Starting graceful restart of model workers to pick correct tokenizer.

raj (sre): I've pushed a temporary scaling policy to dedicated pool to absorb traffic and avoid noisy neighbouring tenants.

julia (support): telling affected customers we have an active mitigation: rolling back catalog default and enabling a safe routing. Will follow up with PS ticket.

sara (oncall): Monitoring: error rate dropped 40% in 5m, 80% in 12m. Latency back to baseline for most routes. Any remaining 500s?

mike (eng-runtime): A few stragglers from older sessions that had cached tokenizer metadata. We're invalidating KV caches for active nodes: 
```
for host in $(list-affected-hosts); do ssh $host 'curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/invalidate_kvcache'; done
```

mike (eng-runtime): KV cache invalidation done. No new tokenizer errors in logs for last 3m.

raj (sre): Resource note: temporary dedicated capacity increased cost by ~12% for the hour. Logged to incident cost bucket.

alice (platform): Added incident annotation to catalog: emergency revert, reason: automated promotion pushed incompatible revision (release pipeline bug). Filed internal PR to block auto-promote until validator covers tokenizer_version.

sara (oncall): Summary for postmortem:
- Trigger: catalog_validator fired (revision mismatch between default and pinned revisions) -> PD P1.
- Root cause: release automation auto-promoted revision rev-2026-03-14 without matching tokenizer compatibility checks.
- Impact: increased 500s, truncated/invalid outputs for some customers, ~27 support tickets, one enterprise with failed requests.
- Mitigation: emergency revert of default_revision, set emergency flag, kicked reconciler & invalidated KV caches, scaled dedicated pool.
- Next steps: add tokenizer_version gate to catalog promotion, add do-not-auto-upgrade guard in catalog metadata, improve alert runbooks with clear rollback playbook.

julia (support): I'll draft customer-facing update once we pass a 30m clean window.

mike (eng-runtime): logs look clean, CPU/mem normalized. No further errors in the last 20m.

sara (oncall): I'll hand off to mike for post-incident follow up. Thanks all. Starting on-call rotation handoff note -> @mike now owning postmortem.

mike (eng-runtime): ack. I'll collect telemetry, add timeline, and create the postmortem doc.

incident-bot: Incident PD-872341 acknowledged by sara. Status: mitigated -> monitoring.

julia (support): Customer update sent to enterprise contact. They confirmed degraded but now stable.

sara (oncall): closing thread for active mitigation. Will reopen if we see regression. :lock:
